use /lib
from /scope/project-directory import ProjectDirectoryScope
from /ui/components/file-browser import FileBrowserScope
from /ui/components/inset-panel import InsetPanelScope

export scope OpenProjectScope:
    concept: {OpenProjectConcept}

concept OpenProjectConcept:
    pitch:
        Opens an existing Piton project by choosing its piton.config.pi, making
        the folder holding it the @{ProjectDirectoryScope}.

    shape: {OpenProjectShape}

shape OpenProjectShape:
    description:
        A @{FileBrowserScope} in an @{InsetPanelScope} over the main window,
        not the platform's own dialog, titled
        "Open a project: choose its piton.config.pi", listing only files named
        piton.config.pi among the folders.

    opening:
        It opens from whatever command opens a project, such as the ribbon's
        Open Project or the palette's "Open Project…", in place of anything
        else in the inset panel. It starts in the folder holding the open
        project, or the home folder when none is open. Opening it while it is
        already open leaves it as it is.

    choosing:
        Choosing a piton.config.pi closes the panel, and the folder holding it
        becomes the project directory for the session.

    cancelling:
        Cancelling, or closing the panel any way an inset panel closes, changes
        nothing.
EOF

commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

content.text:
Open Project now has its own spec scope, `OpenProjectScope`, at `spec/scope/project/open-project/index.pi`, and the code follows the same layout. All tests pass (174, 1 ignored).

**New scope:** it describes the file browser in an inset panel that lists only `piton.config.pi` files. Its sections cover:
- **Opening:** from the ribbon or the palette. It starts in the folder holding the open project, or your home folder, and opening it again changes nothing.
- **Choosing:** the folder holding the chosen file becomes the project.
- **Cancelling:** changes nothing.

**Other spec changes:**
- **`ProjectDirectoryScope`:** now only describes the stored project folder, set by Open Project or New Project. Its picker description moved to the new scope.
- **Ribbon Project tab:** the Open Project button just says it opens `OpenProjectScope`. I also dropped an outdated line about the picker showing errors as a notification, which no longer applies.
- **Palette:** "Open Project…" references the new scope.
- **Main window:** there's a new `openProject` entry.
- **New Project:** a created project opens as if opened with `OpenProjectScope`.

**Code:** a new `src/project/open_project.rs` holds the `OpenProject` action, the browser setup and opening the chosen project. The main window and ribbon use it, and `src/project_directory.rs` is back to just storing the folder. Behaviour is unchanged.

I left New Project where it is, at `spec/scope/new-project`. Say if you want it moved under `project/` alongside Open Project.

`piton check`, `piton build check` and `piton build` ran cleanly, the new `OpenProjectScope.md` reference was generated, and the app builds with no warnings.
